newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil 1997 wheat crop may fall 38 pct - Safras.
newsitem.headline: Brazil 1997 wheat crop may fall 38 pct - Safras.

text.p: Brazilian wheat output in 1997 may fall 38 percent to 1.87 million tonnes from this year's 3.04 million, said consultants Safras e Mercado in its first estimate of the 1997 grains and oilseeds crop.

The sharp fall is due to expectations of a drop in planted area given investments by producers in 1996 are not likely to be returned, partly because of the fall in prices and partly because of rains which have hit the quality of the harvest.

The Brazilian government has made much of the size of this year's wheat harvest which it sees at 3.17 million tonnes, representing a dramatic improvement on last year's 1.5 million to 1.6 million tonnes.
The main reason for the increased plantings was the high international prices prevailing at the time due to supply tightness.

However expectations of dramatically increased world supply in the 1996/97 crop year especially from Mercosul partner Argentina has pushed prices the other way, to the extent that Brazilian farmers are concerned they will not be able to sell the crop at the government minimum price of 157 reais ($153.92).

The government has therefore devised a system in which millers will compete to buy wheat in electronic auctions which set not the outright price but the level of a subsidy to be paid by the government.
The buyer then pays the government the fixed minimum price of 157 reais ($153.92) minus the subsidy set in the auction while the government pays the farmer the full 157 reais.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
